context: Wire the existing 'todo verify --run' path into the completion gate: refuse completion when any rung exits non-zero, with an explicit override flag that records the override and its reason in the events table rather than silently allowing it. Treat pytest exit 5 (no tests collected) as failure, since a vacuous -k selector is the most common way a rung stops testing anything -- the clickhouse-profile-late-binding item already documents that exact trap in its own rung text.
description: BenchBox's active wrapper delegates lifecycle commands to the released todo-db package, whose complete command checks work units, deferrals, and blocks but does not execute the item's verification ladder. That lets completion accept failing or vacuous commands, including pytest exit 5 from an empty selector. Implement the gate in the canonical todo-db package so every consumer gets the same behavior: run the current ladder in order before completion, fail closed on any non-zero or indeterminate result, preserve the hosted-command trust boundary, and provide an explicit reason-bearing override recorded in the completion audit event. Existing done items stay terminal and are not retroactively reopened.

preserves.behavior: Existing completed items are not retroactively reopened by the new gate; it applies to completions from the change forward.
The override path stays available for rungs that genuinely cannot run in a given environment, but records who overrode and why.

work_units.evidence: TodoTracker.complete now runs the current ladder, revalidates its definition and passing results in the completion transaction, preserves the hosted trust gate, and writes reason-bearing override detail into the complete audit event; focused tracker tests passed.
work_units.summary: Implement fail-closed verification execution and audited reason-bearing override in TodoTracker.complete
